content.thinking:
Checking the root-cause claim against the findings: the flag isn't mapped in this repository, which matches the evidence behind the monthly reconciliation totals, so the conclusion is still tentative.

I'm checking whether the spend-integrity alert actually ties to the reconciliation function, since the record shows the alert on shopper totals but doesn't name that function or a monthly window, so that link is still unconfirmed.

I'm checking the causal chain's claim that the flag switching on stopped purchases from reaching the stored monthly total; the record suggests that but doesn't confirm it, so that's still open. The metrics window looks clean, with no other change and no error rate before the onset.

I'm checking the remaining follow-up items, including a proposed repair script, though I'm not judging the action items themselves.

flags.quote: That check compares each account's stored monthly total with the sum of its current-month purchases.
flags.why: The record says the spend-integrity check finds shopper totals that do not reconcile with their purchases, but nowhere ties it to reconcile_monthly_totals or to current-month purchases.

flags.quote: The totals fell short because the feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at {P1.1}, just before the onset at {began}, and from then on purchases were not added to the stored monthly total.
flags.why: The record treats the flag change only as a suspected candidate cause (C1/C2, never tested) and the unwritten monthly total as Code-Fix's untested reading, but this sentence states both as established cause.

supported.quote: When `record_a_purchase` is called with `derive_the_month=True`, it hands the write to `record_purchase_deriving_the_month`, which adds the purchase to the history and moves `total_cents` but never writes `total_this_month_cents`, and raises nothing.
Each purchase written that way leaves the stored monthly total one sale further behind the purchases that `reconcile_monthly_totals` adds up.
The files Code-Fix read do not map the flag monthly-spend-feature to `derive_the_month`, so the record does not show that the flag picks this path.
It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

After a new monthly-spend feature was switched on, the shop likely began recording each purchase without adding it to the shopper's stored total for the month, so those totals fell further behind with every purchase.

Monthly spend totals already stored short stay wrong, and while the flag stays on each new purchase can push another shopper's total further behind, so monthly statements and per-item spend averages read from those totals can show wrong figures.
Stored shopper monthly spend totals fell short of the purchases behind them
Stored shopper spend totals stopped matching the purchases behind them, falling short. The spend-integrity check found this, not a shopper.
The windows read held no other change.
The metrics read do not reach back before the onset, so the service was never measured healthy with any earlier change in place.
rows: Error rate: not measured by the metrics

supported.quote: Any other flag change: the flag provider's history shows no other change by anyone but Argus.
With the flag on, purchases were likely written through a path that moves the shopper's lifetime total but never the stored monthly total.
The only check that compares stored spend totals with their purchases, the spend-integrity check, runs once every {A5} days, and no faster signal of this disagreement was seen.
No check was seen, before the flag went on, that purchases written through the month-deriving path leave the stored monthly total in line with the purchases.
The SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert pages nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
